title: Apollo 11: A Giant Leap for Mankind

lines.text: In July 1969, NASA's Apollo 11 mission made history by landing humans on the Moon.
The mission was crewed by Commander Neil Armstrong, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins, and Lunar Module Pilot Edwin 'Buzz' Aldrin.
lines.image_keyword: Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong Buzz Aldrin

lines.text: Launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on July 16th, the Apollo spacecraft consisted of three parts: the command module, service module, and lunar module.
lines.image_keyword: Saturn V rocket Kennedy Space Center

lines.text: After a three-day transit, Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the surface aboard the lunar module Eagle, landing in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20th.
Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon, followed by Aldrin nineteen minutes later.
lines.image_keyword: Neil Armstrong Apollo 11 moon surface flag

lines.text: Together they spent around two and a half hours walking on the surface, planting an American flag, speaking by telephone with President Richard Nixon, deploying scientific instruments, and collecting lunar material.
The mission's success marked a major achievement for NASA and the United States, fulfilling President John F. Kennedy's challenge to land a man on the Moon before the end of the decade.
The Apollo 11 mission also marked a historic moment in the Space Race between the United States and the Soviet Union.
